title: Selyth Acceptance Policy
description: A content-addressed, human-approved specification of what evidence a change must carry before it is accepted. Policies are data, never code. The engine's behaviour on a given (policy, report) pair is a total function, so the same inputs always produce the same decision and the policy can be read, reviewed and diffed like any other source artifact.

approved_by.description: Human principal accountable for this policy. Required because 'an agent may not weaken acceptance policies' is unenforceable when no human is named as the author of the policy.

rules.description: Evaluated in order; the first matching rule with a terminal action decides. A policy with no rules accepts everything, so rules must be non-empty.

suppression.description: Constraints on human-authored exceptions. Deliberately restrictive: suppression is the mechanism by which a policy is weakened in practice, so it is the mechanism that gets the tightest rules.

mode.description: 'forbidden' in V0.1. Narrowing and deletion are both off the table until the evaluation in docs/roadmap/core-v0.1.md has measured whether a restricted form is needed at all.

recorded_in_report.description: Whether applied suppressions must be listed in the report. A suppression that leaves no trace is indistinguishable from a bug.

on_unknown_evidence.description: What happens when an obligation was never run. Failing open here would mean a skipped check is indistinguishable from a satisfied one.

cost_budget.description: Ceilings that keep the gate inside human attention. A verification gate that takes minutes will be bypassed, and the bypass will not be visible in the report.

paths.description: Path prefixes. Note the limitation recorded in docs/architecture/security-model.md: path matching is advisory in V0.1, because an agent that can move code can move it across a path boundary.

min_evidence_kind.description: Minimum position on the policy's own evidence_lattice.

requires_intent_corroboration.description: Demand an llm-corroborated evidence entry for the intent statement. The intent check is probabilistic and can therefore never satisfy a rule on its own, but it can be required as an additional condition.

non_empty_assumptions.description: Reject proofs that rest on unstated premises. False in V0.1, because a strict reading makes most real proofs unusable; tracked as an open question.

then.description: An escalation that names nobody is a rejection with worse ergonomics.
